profile.address: 10, Teleport Drive, Staten Island, Richmond County, New York, 10314
profile.reading:
The building at 10 Teleport Drive sits within the Staten Island Teleport, a roughly 100-acre technology and business park in the Bloomfield section of Staten Island that New York City and the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey developed in the mid-1980s. The park was originally built around a cluster of satellite dishes serving early transatlantic and domestic data links, and it grew through the 1990s into a hub for telecommunications carriers, broadcasters, and financial-services back-office operations that needed high-bandwidth connectivity outside Manhattan.

By the late 1990s, trade coverage of the Teleport described Merrill Lynch as operating its worldwide data center on the campus, alongside tenants that included Empire Blue Cross Blue Shield and the Industrial Bank of Japan - AT&T, with roughly 198,000 square feet and over 1,000 employees, was then the park's largest occupant. Property tax records for the parcel list two structures at 10 Teleport Drive, identified as 10A and 10B, carried under the Merrill Lynch name, consistent with that trade-press reporting. The building itself, per commercial property records, is a roughly 200,000-square-foot, two-story office structure built in 1990 on a lot of about 438,600 square feet (New York City tax block 2165, lot 35), with a 2025-2026 assessed value of about $13.9 million against a market value near $30.8 million.

The Staten Island site's significance to Merrill Lynch became public in the aftermath of the September 11, 2001 attacks, which destroyed the firm's data centers at the World Financial Center in lower Manhattan. In interviews given afterward, Merrill Lynch's technology leadership described moving the firm's primary data processing to the Staten Island facility, run on a power grid separate from the damaged Manhattan site, while the rebuilt World Financial Center location was reconfigured to serve as a backup rather than the primary facility. That reporting is the clearest public confirmation that this address functioned as a production data center for the firm rather than only a disaster-recovery annex.

Merrill Lynch itself ceased to exist as an independent company when Bank of America completed its acquisition on January 1, 2009, a deal struck at the height of the 2008 financial crisis. The Merrill Lynch and Merrill brand names have continued in use within Bank of America's wealth-management business since then. What has not been made public is whether Bank of America still operates a data center at this Staten Island address today, what its current capacity or tenancy looks like, or whether the site has been repurposed, sold, or folded into Bank of America's broader technology footprint since the 2009 merger. No current operator statement, permit record, or trade coverage found in researching this entry addresses the facility's present-day status.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Merrill Lynch was a major independent investment bank and wealth management firm before Bank of America acquired it in a deal announced in September 2008 amid the global financial crisis, with the transaction closing January 1, 2009. Rather than disappearing, the Merrill Lynch name and the shorter Merrill brand have continued to operate within Bank of Americas wealth management division in the years since, similar in pattern to how AT&T Corp and CenturyLink continued operating as legacy names within larger corporate structures elsewhere in this registry, though this registry has not established that Merrill Lynchs New York data center facility is the same underlying legal entity relationship as those cross-linked duplicate cases, so no duplicate_of link has been applied here. This registrys search for facility-level detail on Merrill Lynchs New York data center returned primarily Bank of America retail banking branch locations rather than data center infrastructure information, so the facilitys specific address, capacity, and technical specifications remain not published as of the research date. Consistent with other financial institutions in this registry, this facility is presumed to support internal banking and wealth management technology operations rather than functioning as commercial colocation space. reading.body:
This facility's specifications for IT capacity, power delivery, cooling systems, and grid connection are not published. The only verified fact is its address on Staten Island. Without published power or rack density figures, this campus cannot be evaluated for its role in AI infrastructure scaling.

New York state has 31 mapped data center facilities, but only one publishes power capacity figures, totaling 3 MW across the state. This facility ranks second by published megawatts, but that ranking reflects absence of data rather than confirmed scale. The state context suggests most facilities in the registry operate without disclosing their technical specifications.

The facility is presumed to support internal Merrill Lynch and Bank of America banking operations rather than commercial colocation. Until specifications are published, this campus has no measurable relevance to decisions about AI compute availability or grid constraint.
